blocks.title: Fully Offline
blocks.text: In vendor mode the network and the module cache are never touched — no proxy, no `go.sum` verification.

items: Only packages actually imported, not whole modules
Tests of dependencies are never copied
`vendor/modules.txt` records paths, versions, go lines
`## explicit` marks a direct requirement
Stale `modules.txt` vs `go.mod` fails the build

left.title: Pros
items: hermetic, offline builds
survives upstream deletion
dep diff reviewable in PRs

right.title: Cons
items: repo bloat, noisy diffs
re-vendor after each change
drifts out of date easily
Non-Go assets not needed to build are dropped
Breaks deps relying on embedded testdata or generated files
`replace` is resolved at vendor time and baked in
Vendored trees never re-apply replaces afresh
Vendor and workspaces interact poorly — use `go work vendor`
Real cases: airgapped builds, vendor-review compliance
Modern alternative: a private proxy (Athens, Artifactory)

blocks.title: One Line
blocks.text: Vendoring buys hermetic builds and pays in repo weight plus permanent upkeep.

lines: package main // blank line above is required

items: Constraint sits above `package`, on its own line
Only blank lines and other comments may follow it
Grammar: `&&`, `||`, `!`, parentheses — a real expression

blocks.title: Legacy Form
items: `// +build linux,amd64` — comma = AND
space = OR, `!` = NOT
1.17+ writes both forms; 1.18+ needs only the new one
`gofmt` syncs them — never hand-edit one alone
Only GOOS and GOARCH values count as suffixes
Test files combine them: `file_windows_test.go`
GOOS, GOARCH, `cgo`, `gc` / `gccgo`, `unix` (1.19+)
Every `go1.N` up to the current release
`go1.21` is cumulative — Go 1.22 satisfies it too
Custom ones: `go build -tags=integration,jsoniter`
Comma-separated list; older Go took spaces instead
Custom tags are set nowhere else — only by that flag

lines: // gen.go, run by //go:generate go run gen.go

items: `ignore` is simply a tag that nobody ever sets
So the file is skipped by every normal build

blocks.title: Tidy Blind Spot
items: Excluded files are invisible to `go mod tidy`'s scan
Their imports can vanish from `go.mod`
Tidy covers all GOOS/GOARCH but NOT custom tags
Fix: a `tools.go` with a tag plus explicit imports
`go list -tags=integration ./...` needs the same tags
So does `go vet -tags=...`, or it analyses another program

blocks.title: The Silent Mistake
blocks.text: No blank line after `//go:build` makes it a doc comment — the file then compiles everywhere.

items: `go mod tidy` adds every missing require, drops every unused one
It is the only correct way to prune the graph
`go mod tidy -go=1.21` rewrites the go line and re-prunes
Commit `go.mod` and `go.sum` in the same commit

lines: go get a.com/dep@v1.5.0    # edits deps only

items: Since Go 1.22 `go get` no longer installs binaries
`go install pkg@version` ignores the current `go.mod`
Pin tools in `tools.go` behind `//go:build tools`
Then tidy keeps their versions pinned for you

lines: go mod tidy && git diff --exit-code go.mod

items: `go mod download` warms the cache before the build
`-mod=readonly` fails instead of editing `go.mod` for you
The tidy diff guard fails the build on an untidy tree
`go mod verify` re-hashes the cache against `go.sum`
Stale sums: `go mod download <mod>` or just tidy
Private: `GOPRIVATE=github.com/org/*` plus a credential helper
Or an `insteadOf` SSH rewrite in `.gitconfig`
Use `go.work` instead of a committed local `replace`

blocks.title: Never Delete go.sum
blocks.text: Regenerating it just trusts whatever the network serves today. Investigate the mismatch instead.

blocks.title: Upgrade Narrowly
blocks.text: `go get -u ./...` bumps everything at once. Prefer targeted upgrades and read the release notes.

items: A downgrade can force other modules down with it
`@latest` skips prereleases and retracted versions

blocks.q: Something is in my build and I don't know why.
a_bullets: `go list -m all` — which version got selected
`go mod why -m X` — shortest path keeping it in
`go mod graph` — who required it, edge by edge

items: Read it top-down: your module, then the chain to the dep
`b.com/lib` is the real owner — upgrade there, not here
`go mod graph | grep x/text` shows every version required
MVS then keeps the highest of those minimums

blocks.title: Whole Handbook, One Line
blocks.text: `go.mod` = minimums, `go.sum` = integrity, MVS = highest-of-minimums, `/vN` = major in path, vendor = hermetic copy, build tags = which files exist at all.

caption.text: Part 2 of GO MODULES. Every Go build you ship is decided by two text files and one algorithm that picks the LOWEST version that works — the opposite of npm. Ten pages on go.mod internals, pseudo-versions, semantic import versioning, MVS, the checksum database, replace/retract, vendoring and build tags. Save it for the next time `checksum mismatch` ruins your afternoon.
